chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan narrated to us, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from 'Umar A'dinah, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

The one who does like what was done to him, has only acted equivalently; and the one who multiplies (the good), is thankful; and the one who is thankful, is generous. The one who knows that what was done to him was only done to himself, will not delay thanking people, nor increase affection to them. Know that the one who seeks a need from you has not considered himself dignified above you, hence, dignify yourself from refusing him.

key_terms.أَضْعَفَ: To multiply or increase (the good deed beyond equivalence).
key_terms.شَاكِرًا: Thankful (grateful for the opportunity to give).
key_terms.كَافَأَ: To act equivalently or reciprocate equally.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between equivalence and thankfulness in giving, and how should one treat those who ask for favors?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between mere reciprocity (*kafa'ah*) and true generosity (*shukr*), emphasizing that recognizing the intrinsic benefit of blessings to the self fosters sincere gratitude. The text further links social etiquette to spiritual humility, noting that the petitioner’s self-abasement should be met with the benefactor’s dignified response, reflecting the Shia ethical principle of *ihsan* (excellence in conduct). This teaching underscores the interplay between divine grace and human social responsibility in maintaining communal bonds.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father (ra) that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Isa bin Ubaid, that he said: We were told by Ubaidullah bin Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Darast bin Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Umar bin Udhayna, from Zurara, that he said: I heard Abu Ja’far (AS) say:

The one who does like what was done to him, has only acted equivalently; and the one who multiplies, is thankful; and the one who is thankful, is generous. The one who knows that what was done to him was only done to himself, will not delay thanking people, nor increase affection to them. Know that the one who seeks a need from you has not considered himself dignified above you, hence, dignify yourself from refusing him.
